title: Game of Thrones: Mad King Debuts at Royal Shakespeare
seoTitle: Mad King Returns in New Game of Thrones Stage Prequel
subtitle: Jousts, dry ice and fire shape the theatrical prequel that brings tyrant Aerys II to the stage
excerpt: At the Royal Shakespeare Theatre, a new Game of Thrones prequel stages the Mad King Aerys II, featuring nonstop jousts, dry‑ice fog and flames, linking the TV saga to the stage.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Royal Shakespeare Theatre, Stratford-upon-Avon – The Royal Shakespeare Company’s stage welcomes a new prequel to the famous TV series, bringing the figure of the Mad King, Aerys II Targaryen, to the theatre.

An Action-Packed Saga with Visual Effects

According to the review, the production stands out for an endless sequence of jousts, where knights clash in lance duels that fill the set with rhythm and energy. The show also employs dry ice and fire, creating a visual environment that blends ethereal cold with the heat of battle, reinforcing the tension‑filled atmosphere that permeates Aerys II’s story.

Stage Spectacle and Contemporary Resonance

The stage effects are described as spectacular, indicating that the production uses advanced technical resources to turn the theatre space into a medieval battlefield. Beyond the visual grandeur, the play offers a “modern resonance,” suggesting that themes of power, tyranny and rebellion remain relevant for today’s audiences.

Context Within the Royal Shakespeare Company

Across the 65‑year history of the Royal Shakespeare Company, numerous incarnations of characters such as Lear and Caesar have been presented, often marked by madness and courtly violence. The Mad King fits into this tradition, presenting a tyrant whose fate mirrors those of historical and literary figures already explored in the company’s repertoire.

The Central Character

Aerys II Targaryen, described as an ancestor of a bloody lineage featured in Game of Thrones, takes centre stage. His figure, as a new tyrant on the RSC’s boards, connects the television narrative to the theatrical universe, offering audiences an expanded view of the saga created by George R.R. Martin in “A Song of Ice…”.

In summary, the review highlights that the new production combines constant action, dry‑ice and fire effects, and an approach that engages with contemporary issues, all within the 65‑year tradition of the Royal Shakespeare Company.

With information from The Guardian.
